sources.note: A sequence of mathematical peer corrections converging on the frozen KR-REP-REDUCTION-2026-09 formal protocol. Fixes an indexing inconsistency to the clean chain R5=T5(D), R_{n-1}=T_n(R_n) for n=5..2, giving D->R5->R4->R3->R2->R1; replaces a too-strong requirement of strictly decreasing entropy H(R_n)<H(R_{n+1}) with strictly decreasing representation CAPACITY, keeping entropy an independently measured, non-monotone quantity; distinguishes empirical/observed adequacy (H_hat(Q|R_n)=0, a claim about the tested sample) from theoretical/population adequacy (H(Q|R_n)=0), adding the fiber-violation count N_viol(R_n) as an equivalent, more auditable structural diagnostic (N_viol=0 iff H_hat(Q|R)=0 on finite empirical support, though the two serve different diagnostic roles -- structural witness vs information summary); redefines the minimal adequate level not as argmin H(R_n) but as the boundary n*=min{n: A(R_n)=1, N_viol(R_n)=0, H_hat(Q|R_n)=0}, explicitly requiring the definition to name that R_{n*-1} actually fails and warning that if adequacy is non-monotone across the chain, the complete adequacy profile must be reported rather than a single boundary; measures both H(Q|R_n) (sufficiency) and H(R_n|Q) (renamed 'Q-relative residual representation,' never 'excess,' since residual distinctions such as provenance/uncertainty/lineage may be intentionally preserved by Pi even when Q-extraneous); derives the central decomposition identity H(T)=H(Q)+H(T|Q) for adequate deterministic T, hence H(T)>=H(Q) with equality iff H(T|Q)=0; corrects a proposed 'Q-isomorphic representation' (Level 4) to 'Q-equivalent representation' (mutual a.s. recoverability H(Q|T)=H(T|Q)=0), since factorization Q=O∘T alone does not establish a bijection; separates three independent boundary-failure diagnostic dimensions (Representation boundary: N_viol>0 or H(Q|R)>0; Contract boundary: A(R)<1; Operator boundary: H(Q|R)=0 but F(R)<1) explicitly allowed to co-occur rather than being mutually exclusive categories; and freezes the invariant Adequacy != Realization != Minimality != Q-equivalence together with the final measurement vector M_n=(A_n,F_n,H_hat(Q|R_n),H_hat(R_n|Q),H_hat(R_n),N_viol,n) as the canonical KR-REP-REDUCTION experimental protocol, explicitly deferring a controlled 2x2 (T_extreme/T_realistic x Pi_extreme/Pi_realistic) test of transformation-preservation interaction to a later stage.

rows.anchor: N_viol(R)=0 <=> H_hat(Q|R)=0, not merely N_viol=0 => H_hat(Q|R)=0 ... The asymmetry is diagnostic rather than logical.
rows.statement: Strengthens a stated implication into a full equivalence: for finite empirical support, N_viol(R)=0 and H_hat(Q|R)=0 are logically equivalent adequacy conditions (since zero conditional entropy forces every observed R-fiber to a single Q-value and vice versa), but the two remain diagnostically distinct -- N_viol as a structural witness locating collisions, H_hat(Q|R) as an information summary of remaining uncertainty.

rows.anchor: R_{n*} is adequate, R_{n*-1} is inadequate, B_{n*}: R_{n*} -> R_{n*-1}. If adequacy is non-monotone across the chain, record that as an experimental finding rather than assuming a single boundary.
rows.statement: Requires the boundary transition B_{n*} to be defined only when both the adjacency condition (R_{n*} adequate) and its failure (R_{n*-1} inadequate) are established, distinguishing 'lowest adequate level,' 'first preservation failure,' and 'boundary transition' as three concepts that coincide only under monotone preservation behaviour across the reduction chain.

rows.anchor: H(R|Q)>0 => R contains variation not determined by Q ... This variation is Q-extraneous relative to the inquiry, but is not necessarily useless information.
rows.statement: Refines the interpretation of H(R|Q)>0 from 'R contains non-inquiry payload' to the more precise 'R contains variation not determined by Q,' explicitly noting this Q-extraneous variation may still be valuable for provenance, auditability, explainability, or answering a different future inquiry -- so H(R|Q)=0 means 'no Q-extraneous variation,' not 'nothing else is useful.'

rows.anchor: A: Is R sufficient? <-> N_viol, H_hat(Q|R). B: Does O realize the contract? <-> A(R), F(R). C: How much Q-extraneous representation remains? <-> H_hat(R|Q). D: Where does reduction cross the boundary? <-> n*.
rows.statement: Freezes a four-question decomposition of the KR-REP-REDUCTION protocol (sufficiency, contract realization, excess representation, boundary) each matched to a specific empirical observable (N_viol/H_hat(Q|R); A(R)/F(R); H_hat(R|Q); n*), and separates three independently-diagnosable boundary-failure kinds (Representation Boundary: N_viol>0 or H(Q|R)>0; Contract Boundary: A(R)<1; Operator Boundary: H(Q|R)=0 but F(R)<1), noting 'information was lost != contract was violated != decoder was inadequate' as three genuinely different failure modes that a reduction can exhibit.

rows.anchor: A two-state representation can have entropy close to 1 bit, while a larger representation can have much lower entropy if its distribution is highly concentrated. ... distinguish representation capacity, storage cost, Shannon entropy, minimality.
rows.statement: Rejects a proposed requirement of strictly decreasing entropy H(R_n)<H(R_{n+1}) across the reduction chain as too strong, since entropy depends on the induced probability distribution rather than representation size; recommends requiring strictly decreasing representation CAPACITY instead, and measuring entropy, storage cost, and minimality as independent, separately reported quantities.

rows.anchor: A failed representation transition Rn -> Rn-1 demonstrates that the transformation does not preserve the contract for that sample. It does not automatically identify a unique payload S that was removed.
rows.statement: Warns against over-interpreting a failed reduction step: multiple eliminated components, interaction effects, transformation-induced changes, recombination, or loss of relational structure could all produce the same observed failure, so a specific eliminated set S notin Elim_{T,Pi}(D) may only be inferred when T_n has an explicit, declared elimination decomposition T_n=E_{S_n} -- otherwise report only 'T_n crosses the preservation boundary for D_i,' connecting this directly to the KR-ZERO-ORDER finding that transformation loss should not be assumed to decompose element-wise.

rows.anchor: H(T)=H(Q)+H(T|Q), therefore H(T)>=H(Q), with equality iff H(T|Q)=0 ... T(D) = G(Q(D)) almost surely ... T(D) and Q(D) are mutually deterministically recoverable almost surely.
rows.statement: Confirms Theorem 3's corrected attainability condition H(T(D)|Q(D))=0 and its consequence H(T)=H(Q)+H(T|Q); corrects the proposed 'Level 4: Q-Isomorphic Representation' (from Q=O∘T alone) to 'Q-Equivalent Representation,' since factorization through T establishes only that T contains enough information to determine Q, not a bijection between the full codomains Y and Q-space; the stronger, correct claim requires both H(Q(D)|T(D))=0 and H(T(D)|Q(D))=0, giving mutual a.s. recoverability T(D) <-> Q(D) rather than an unproven isomorphism.

rows.anchor: sim_{Pi,T} = sim_Q restricted to X_{Pi,T} ... T(D) cannot literally be an element of [D]_{sim_Pi} ... D sim_{Pi,T} E_S(D) because Q(D)=Q(E_S(D)).
rows.statement: Repairs two structural errors: (1) the equivalence relation sim_Pi must be defined as the global Q-induced relation sim_Q restricted to the T-dependent admissible domain X_{Pi,T}, not as an independent relation whose domain and defining condition are conflated; (2) a 'same fiber' claim mixing source-space [D]_{sim_Pi} (subset of X) with representation-space elements T(D), T(E_S(D)) (elements of Y) is type-incorrect -- the correct statement is D sim_{Pi,T} E_S(D) in source space, with O(T(D))=O(T(E_S(D))) as the separate representation-space consequence.

rows.anchor: T_Adeq(Q) = {T: H(Q(D)|T(D))=0} ... T_Real(Pi) = {T: P(D in X_{Pi,T})=1 and P(O(T(D))=Q(D))=1}.
rows.statement: Separates a previously ambiguous family T_adequate(Pi) into two explicitly distinct families -- T_Adeq(Q) (transformations adequate for the inquiry alone) and T_Real(Pi) (transformations that additionally realize the whole contract, both admissibility and the fixed decoder) -- and cautions that entropy minimization T*=argmin H(T(D)) should be stated as an infimum unless existence of the minimizer is separately established.

rows.anchor: Zero_{T_n,Pi}(S_n;R^n) => Adeq(R^{n-1},Q,Pi) as the Zero-boundary hypothesis. I would not formulate it that strongly anymore ... Zero is itself a judgment produced by (D,T,Pi,S).
rows.statement: Rejects a proposed strong 'Zero-boundary hypothesis' (Zero at a reduction step implies adequacy of the next representation) as formulated too strongly, arguing instead that Zero is one observable judgment produced by the underlying tuple (D,T,Pi,S), with an unnamed interaction structure I_{T,Pi}(D,S) as the real open mathematical object -- reframing the research question from 'what does Zero predict?' to 'what structure determines the boundary at which reduction ceases to preserve the contract, of which Zero is one detection mechanism?'

rows.anchor: KR-ZERO discovered empirical constraints on context-dependent eliminability and revealed that relational structure may enter through the transformation/preservation pair. KR-REP-REDUCTION now independently investigates representation reduction ... using the KR-ZERO findings as controlled experimental factors and hypotheses -- not as definitions or conclusions.
rows.statement: Revises the relationship between the two experiment families: rather than 'KR-ZERO discovers eliminability; KR-REP-REDUCTION tests whether Zero predicts adequacy,' the corrected position is that KR-ZERO's findings become controlled experimental factors and hypotheses for KR-REP-REDUCTION, never definitions or conclusions it inherits; elevates the representation carrier (individual element vs subset vs relational structure/hypergraph/rewriting state) to a first-class unresolved research question that must be settled before R5->R2 can be properly designed.

rows.anchor: Adequacy != Contract Realization ... otherwise a representation could look mathematically sufficient while failing the actual preservation/operational contract.
rows.statement: Adopts Adequacy != Contract Realization as a hard experimental rule for KR-REP-REDUCTION, distinguishing T_Adeq(Q) (sufficient information exists) from T_Real(Pi) (the specified operator O actually realizes it, and admissibility holds), so that a mathematically sufficient representation is never conflated with one that actually satisfies the operational contract.

rows.anchor: KR-ZERO: When can source material be eliminated while preserving the contract? KR-REP-REDUCTION: How far can the representation be reduced while retaining inquiry adequacy and contract realization? The bridge is a hypothesis to test, not an established implication.
rows.statement: States the final, precise research-question separation between the two experiment families and explicitly classifies the connecting arrow (Zero_{T_n,Pi} -> candidate elimination -> R^{n-1} -> Adequacy/Realization) as a hypothesis to be tested by KR-REP-REDUCTION, never an established implication inherited from KR-ZERO; freezes a status ledger distinguishing [CORPUS] established facts, [EXP] established mathematical results (H(Q|T)=0 adequacy; H(T|Q)=0 no-excess; hence H(T)=H(Q)+H(T|Q)), [PROP] proposed measures (Excess_Q(T)=H(T|Q); Zero predicting adequacy), and five explicit [OPEN] questions (existence of a general R5->R2 chain; the representation carrier; monotonicity; whether Zero predicts the boundary; whether relational structure in T,Pi predicts reduction difficulty).

rows.anchor: X_Q(R) = H(R|Q) as Q-relative residual representation, with excess representation as an interpretation only when the contract explicitly says those distinctions are unnecessary.
rows.statement: Names the final residual-representation quantity X_Q(R)=H(R|Q) as 'Q-relative residual representation,' explicitly reserving the normatively loaded term 'excess representation' only for cases where the preservation contract itself declares the residual distinctions unnecessary, on the principle that what is unnecessary for one inquiry is not thereby unnecessary for every inquiry (provenance, uncertainty bounds, or lineage may be irrelevant to Q while still required by the broader contract Pi).

rows.anchor: R(Q,Pi) = (D, {R_n}, {T_n}, O, Q, Pi) ... M_n = (A_n, F_n, H_hat(Q|R_n), X_Q(R_n), H_hat(R_n), N_viol,n) ... n* = min{n in {1..5} : Comp_n=1.0 and A_n=1.0 and N_viol,n=0 and H_hat(Q|R_n)=0}.
rows.statement: Presents the fully frozen KR-REP-REDUCTION experimental protocol as the object R(Q,Pi)=(D,{R_n},{T_n},O,Q,Pi) with directional chain D->T5->R5->T4->R4->T3->R3->T2->R2->T1->R1, entropy/size/count recorded independently per level (monotonicity treated as an empirical hypothesis, never assumed), a completeness-declared per-level measurement vector M_n=(A_n,F_n,H_hat(Q|R_n),X_Q(R_n),H_hat(R_n),N_viol,n), the closed-form fiber-violation formula N_viol,n=sum_r [(sum_q c_{r,q})^2 - sum_q c_{r,q}^2]/2, and the boundary definition n*=min{n: Comp_n=1, A_n=1, N_viol,n=0, H_hat(Q|R_n)=0}, with R_{n*} confirmed as the chain-specific preservation boundary only if the next-lower level fails at least one of those conditions.

rows.anchor: The current design does not yet fully test H-RR3 (T-Pi interaction) ... the controlled 2x2 experiment is deferred ... the next useful review is of the actual implementation and its FT-1...FT-7 execution results.
rows.statement: Notes that the frozen protocol design defers the controlled 2x2 (T_extreme/realistic x Pi_extreme/realistic) test of transformation-preservation interaction (hypothesis H-RR3), so the design phase can investigate the reduction boundary and observe an association with Zero but cannot yet establish a general T-Pi interaction law; records that the theoretical/protocol design phase is complete and the next required review step is of the actual implementation's FT-1 through FT-7 execution results, i.e. an experiment run beyond the scope of this file.

rows.anchor: Contract failure: NO / Operator-only failure: NO / Representation failure: YES ... A_n = 1.000 at every level ... You need a representation where H(Q|R)=0 while simultaneously O(R)!=Q.
rows.statement: Reports that hypothesis H-B (intending to separate representation failure, contract failure, and operator failure) found only representation failure occurring, since admissibility A_n=1.000 held at every level and the fixed decoder F=1.000 at the only adequate level R5, so no empirical state arose where Q was recoverable from R (H(Q|R)=0) yet the fixed operator O failed to recover Q (O(R)!=Q); concludes that a fixed decoder alone does not create an operator-boundary experiment -- a representation must retain enough information (H(Q|R)=0) while the chosen decoder still fails to use it -- and this chain never produced such a state, so adequacy and realization remain conceptually distinct even though this experiment did not empirically separate them along the reduction chain.

rows.anchor: ascending: F_argmax = 0.8667 / descending: F_argmax = 0.3230 ... a difference of 54.37 percentage points ... yet H(Q|R2) 3.3937 vs 3.3965 is essentially unchanged.
rows.statement: Reports a strong empirical demonstration that representation adequacy is distinct from fixed-decoder realization: reversing a rank encoding convention (ascending vs descending) leaves Hhat(Q|R2) essentially unchanged (3.3937 vs 3.3965) and N_viol similar, yet the fixed decoder's F_argmax swings by 54.37 percentage points (0.8667 vs 0.3230); interprets this as same recoverable information under different encoding convention producing very different fixed-decoder performance, i.e. a representation can preserve the same recoverable information while a particular fixed decoder performs very differently because it interprets the representation differently.

rows.anchor: "A change carrying NO information about D..." ... The ascending and descending rank conventions are information-equivalent recodings of the same rank representation, yet they produce substantially different performance for the fixed decoder O.
rows.statement: Requests softening the phrase 'a change carrying no information about D' to the more formal 'the ascending and descending rank conventions are information-equivalent recodings of the same rank representation, yet they produce substantially different performance for the fixed decoder O', on the ground that what matters theoretically is not an informal claim of 'no information' but that the transformation between conventions is information-preserving/invertible; connects this directly to the project's Q-equivalence concept.

rows.anchor: bytes: 37 -> 37 -> 37 -> 25 / fields: 2 -> 2 -> 2 -> 2 / cardinality: 26826 -> 5696 -> 3288 -> 162 / entropy: 15.04 -> 12.31 -> 11.10 -> 7.17 ... there is no single obvious scalar called "amount of reduction"
rows.statement: Reports the four measured reduction-dimension trajectories (bytes, fields, cardinality, entropy) across R5..R2 and argues the evidence only establishes that no single scalar 'amount of reduction' captures all four dimensions -- i.e. reduction is multidimensional and the measured dimensions do not collapse into one common trajectory -- but four observations along a single chain cannot establish statistical independence, so hypothesis H-D's claim that 'the four dimensions move independently' should be softened to that weaker, corpus-supported statement.

rows.anchor: "H-C refuted a priori." -> "H-C was identified as structurally inapplicable to the specified deterministic sequential chain..." ... "[NEG] The design failed to operationalize the intended separation of representation, contract, and operator boundaries."
rows.statement: Requests two specific wording corrections before any freeze: replacing 'H-C refuted a priori' with language stating H-C was structurally inapplicable to the specified deterministic sequential chain (the data-processing inequality makes empirical monotonicity a chain-consistency check, not an independent test of H-C), and, for H-B, replacing an unqualified 'FALSIFIED' with '[NEG] The design failed to operationalize the intended separation of representation, contract, and operator boundaries; representation failure was observable, contract-only and operator-only failure were not generated' -- attributing the failure to the experimental design rather than to the underlying theoretical distinction.

rows.anchor: R_up =~enc R_down if and only if the implementation demonstrates a bijection between them ... exists f,g: f(R_up)=R_down, g(R_down)=R_up with g o f = id, f o g = id. Only then should we connect this experiment strongly to the existing Q-equivalence research.
rows.statement: Requires that the ascending/descending rank representations only be called equivalent (R_up cong_enc R_down) once the implementation demonstrates an actual bijection f,g between them satisfying g.f=id and f.g=id, and that any residual measured difference in H(Q|R) absent such a bijection be attributed to sampling/estimation or implementation effects rather than treated as evidence of non-equivalence; only a confirmed bijection should connect this result to the existing Q-equivalence research.

rows.anchor: It says H(Q|R5)=0 too strongly ... it correctly acknowledges that the experiment only established Hhat(Q|R5)=0 on the two finite samples, not population H(Q|R5)=0. That is an internal inconsistency. ... No observed training or test collisions were found at R5; this provides empirical evidence consis
rows.statement: Identifies and corrects an internal inconsistency in the reviewed assessment: it states H(Q|R5)=0 too strongly when the experiment only established the empirical/finite-sample quantity Hhat(Q|R5)=0 (no observed training or test collisions), not the population-level H(Q|R5)=0; insists this distinction matters because the project is explicitly trying to maintain the separation between finite-sample evidence and theoretical claims.

rows.anchor: H(R)=H(Q)+H(R|Q) ... calling H(R|Q) 'excess information' would be dangerous ... provenance, audit information, uncertainty, temporal information, identity, reconstruction metadata ... Q-relative residual representation is a much safer concept than excess information.
rows.statement: Re-endorses avoiding the term 'excess information' for H(R|Q) in the decomposition H(R)=H(Q)+H(R|Q), since residual content such as provenance, audit information, uncertainty, temporal information, identity, or reconstruction metadata may be irrelevant to the current Q while being extremely important to another contract, reaffirming 'Q-relative residual representation' as the safer term, especially once the toy numeric carrier is left behind.

rows.anchor: Before calling the two rank representations information-equivalent, the implementation should explicitly establish a bijection f: R_up <-> R_down. If it does, then conditional entropy should theoretically be invariant under that invertible recoding. [AUDIT] Prove the rank-direction transformation is
rows.statement: Reiterates as a formal audit item ([AUDIT] tag) that the rank-direction transformation's bijectivity at the representation level must be proven before the ascending/descending rank representations are called information-equivalent, since a confirmed bijection would make conditional entropy theoretically invariant and reduce the tiny observed difference to an estimator/sample effect.

rows.anchor: I would retain the explicit notation Hhat(Q|R)=0 and never silently promote it to H(Q|R)=0. That distinction should remain mandatory in all future experiment reports.
rows.statement: Makes it a mandatory rule for all future experiment reports that empirical recoverability be notated explicitly as Hhat(Q|R)=0 and never silently promoted to the population claim H(Q|R)=0.

rows.anchor: Define Q BEFORE generating representations. ... Adequate(R) iff Q is recoverable from R. Operationally measure both empirical conditional information Hhat(Q|R) and exact semantic violation count Nviol ... Do not treat Hhat(Q|R)=0 as proof that population H(Q|R)=0.
rows.statement: Requires the preservation target Q to be defined before representations are generated, with adequacy defined as Q being recoverable from R, measured operationally via both empirical conditional information Hhat(Q|R) and an exact semantic violation count Nviol, while never treating the empirical Hhat(Q|R)=0 as proof of the population-level H(Q|R)=0.

rows.anchor: Retain the KR-REP-REDUCTION principle that reduction is multidimensional. Measure independently ... encoded size, cardinality, field count, representation entropy, number of relations, number of records, other declared structural measures. Do NOT invent a single 'reduction score' ... If a decoder is
rows.statement: Requires measuring reduction multidimensionally (encoded size, cardinality, field count, entropy, relation count, record count, other declared measures) without inventing a single reduction score or assuming statistical independence among dimensions, and requires keeping representation adequacy strictly separate from decoder realization when a decoder is used, including an invertible recoding control to rule out decoder-sensitivity confounds.

rows.anchor: Hhat=0 means: zero empirical estimate in the tested sample/experiment. It does not mean H=0 for the entire population ... 'No relationship observed' does not mean 'Independence universally proven.' This distinction must remain embedded in KnowledgeOS governance.
rows.statement: Enshrines the empirical-vs-universal distinction (Hhat=0 meaning only a zero sample estimate, never population H=0; 'no relationship observed' never meaning 'independence universally proven') as a requirement that must remain embedded in KnowledgeOS governance going forward.

rows.anchor: N_viol=0 => empirical adequacy on the tested sample. This does not imply population adequacy. That distinction is fundamental.
rows.statement: Formalizes the finite-sample operational adequacy criterion: a deterministic empirical decoder exists iff every representation value corresponds to at most one inquiry value in the test set (equivalently N_viol=0), which implies only empirical adequacy on the tested sample, never population adequacy.

rows.anchor: Hhat(Q|R)=0 does not establish H(Q|R)=0 in the population. It establishes only a sample-level result under the estimator and observed support. Hhat=0 !=> H=0 without additional statistical assumptions. This distinction is mandatory.
rows.statement: Mandates the population-vs-sample distinction as a formal requirement: the empirical estimator result Hhat(Q|R)=0 establishes only a sample-level result under the given estimator and observed support, never the population-level H(Q|R)=0, without additional statistical assumptions.

rows.anchor: only the last digit and twice the penultimate digit are needed [for divisibility by 4] ... D -> S(D) where S(D) is a much smaller statistic sufficient for the particular question ... R_Q(D) such that Q(D)=g(R_Q(D)) ... the same structural idea as our existing adequacy criterion H(Q(D)|R(D))=0.
rows.statement: Extracts a sufficient-local-statistic pattern from the divisibility-by-4 rule (only the last two digits are needed) as a historical conceptual example matching the existing adequacy criterion H(Q(D)|R(D))=0 -- not proof of the theory, but a strong historical inspiration for question-relative sufficient representation.

rows.anchor: H(D)=n log2(10) bits. D mod 4 = (2 d1 + d0) mod 4. R_Q(D)=(d1,d0) ... I(Q(D);D)=H(Q(D))-H(Q(D)|D)=H(Q(D)). H(Q(D)|R_Q(D))=0. This satisfies the exact mathematical definition of a Minimal Sufficient Statistic R_Q(D) for query Q.
rows.statement: Proves rigorously, via the data-processing inequality, that the divisibility-by-4 example's reduced statistic R_Q(D)=(d1,d0) (last two digits) satisfies H(Q(D)|R_Q(D))=0, the exact mathematical definition of a minimal sufficient statistic for the query Q(D)=[D mod 4==0], with the information-theoretic loss maximal for irrelevant higher digits but zero for the target query.

lexical.anchor: N_viol(R)=0 <=> H_hat(Q|R)=0, not merely N_viol=0 => H_hat(Q|R)=0 ... The asymmetry is diagnostic rather than logical.

conceptual.anchor: only the last digit and twice the penultimate digit are needed [for divisibility by 4] ... D -> S(D) where S(D) is a much smaller statistic sufficient for the particular question ... R_Q(D) such that Q(D)=g(R_Q(D)) ... the same structural idea as our existing adequacy criterion H(Q(D)|R(D))=0.

formal.anchor: A: Is R sufficient? <-> N_viol, H_hat(Q|R). B: Does O realize the contract? <-> A(R), F(R). C: How much Q-extraneous representation remains? <-> H_hat(R|Q). D: Where does reduction cross the boundary? <-> n*.

notations: K_t=(\mathcal A_t,\mathcal E_t,\mathcal R_t,\mathcal C_t,\mathcal H_t,\Gamma_t)

sources.note: S0862's Step 7: rejects K_{t+1}=K_t U e_t; defines K_t as a six-component tuple, eight named transition operations as a partial function, a multidimensional (non-linear-lifecycle) assertion state, event-sourced reconstruction with policy/ontology versioning, three separated time axes, a paraconsistent stance toward P/not-P, a worked four-event example, eight K1-K8 invariants, and explicitly defers the epistemic AcceptancePolicy question to Step 8.

rows.anchor: The fundamental problem ... A naive model would say K_{t+1}=K_t\cup e_t. That is insufficient. ... introduce a new assertion; strengthen; weaken; contradict; resolve a conflict; create a new conflict; invalidate; make stale; change an interpretation; expose that a previous conclusion was unsupported
rows.statement: Rejects the naive model K_{t+1}=K_t∪e_t as insufficient, listing eleven distinct effects new evidence can have (introduce/strengthen/weaken/contradict/resolve/create conflict/invalidate/stale/reinterpret/expose unsupported/reveal new dimension) to establish K_{t+1}≠K_t∪e_t in general.

rows.anchor: What exactly is the Knowledge State? ... K_t=(\mathcal A_t,\mathcal E_t,\mathcal R_t,\mathcal C_t,\mathcal H_t,\Gamma_t) ... Assertions currently represented ... Evidence known to the system ... Relations between knowledge objects ... Active conflicts ... Historical event/state record ... Current co
rows.statement: Defines the Knowledge State as a six-component tuple K_t=(Assertions, Evidence, Relations, ActiveConflicts, History, ContextualConditions), holding not just beliefs but the structure explaining why/under-what-conditions they are held.

rows.anchor: Current state versus history ... K_t \neq H_t ... An assertion may no longer be current while remaining historically important. ... 2024: Nexus = 3.69 ... 2025: Nexus = 3.70 ... 2026: Nexus = 3.85 ... Superseded\neq Deleted
rows.statement: Distinguishes current Knowledge State K_t from historical evolution H_t, illustrated by three successive Nexus-version assertions, concluding Superseded ≠ Deleted.

rows.anchor: Knowledge State transition ... K_{t+1} = \delta_\rho(K_t,e_t) ... the actual transition should be mediated by an epistemic event: K_t \xrightarrow{event_t} K_{t+1} because evidence itself does not directly mutate knowledge.
rows.statement: Refines the transition K_{t+1}=δ_ρ(K_t,e_t) to be mediated by an explicit epistemic event rather than evidence directly mutating knowledge.

rows.anchor: Evidence does not directly change knowledge ... We do not automatically execute K:=K\cup\{Nexus=3.69\}. Instead e \rightarrow Assessment \rightarrow Conclusion \rightarrow KnowledgeStateTransition. Evidence\not\Rightarrow Knowledge ... Evidence \rightarrow EvidenceAssessment \rightarrow EpistemicCon
rows.statement: States the crucial invariant Evidence ⇏ Knowledge: evidence must pass through Assessment and Conclusion stages before touching the Knowledge State, preventing raw LLM output/documents/human statements from silently becoming accepted knowledge.

rows.anchor: The transition pipeline ... e_t \rightarrow EA_t \rightarrow c_t \rightarrow \delta_\rho \rightarrow K_{t+1}
rows.statement: Formalizes the transition pipeline e_t→EA_t (Evidence Assessment)→c_t (conclusion/update proposal)→δ_ρ (state transition policy)→K_{t+1}.

rows.anchor: What operations can happen? ... Introduce(P,e)\rightarrow A ... Corroborate(A,e)\rightarrow A' ... Qualify ... Nexus 3.69 in the legacy environment ... Contradict(A,e)\rightarrow Conflict ... Supersede ... TemporalChange\neq LogicalContradiction ... Resolve(C)\rightarrow ContextualizedAssertions rat
rows.statement: Defines eight named Knowledge-State transition operations: Introduce (new proposition represented), Corroborate (independent supporting evidence strengthens an assertion), Qualify (adds conditions without invalidating), Contradict (produces Conflict, not automatic replacement), Supersede (temporal change ≠ logical contradiction), Resolve (produces contextualized assertions, never silent deletion), Retract (retract ≠ delete, retaining historical status/evidence/provenance), and Invalidate (temporal expiry ≠ retraction).

rows.anchor: The transition algebra ... \mathcal O_K=\{Introduce,Corroborate,Qualify,Contradict,Supersede,Resolve,Retract,Invalidate\} ... \delta: K\times\mathcal O_K \rightharpoonup K ... The arrow is partial ... because not every operation is valid in every state. ... Resolve(C) is invalid if C\notin\mathcal C
rows.statement: Formalizes the transition algebra δ:K×O_K⇀K as a partial function over the eight-operation set O_K, since not every operation is valid in every state (e.g. Resolve(C) is invalid unless C is an active conflict).

rows.anchor: This gives us state-machine semantics ... Do not make this a single linear lifecycle. An assertion's epistemic dimensions are independent. ... State = (Acquisition,Support,Uncertainty,Validity) plus relational state: Conflict, Resolution, Supersession, etc.
rows.statement: Rejects a single linear assertion lifecycle (Unknown→Introduced→Corroborated/Conflicted/Retracted/Superseded) as inadequate since an assertion's epistemic dimensions are independent, proposing instead an independent-dimension State=(Acquisition,Support,Uncertainty,Validity) plus separate relational state (Conflict/Resolution/Supersession).

rows.anchor: Therefore assertion state remains multidimensional ... \Sigma_A=(Acquisition,Support,Uncertainty,Validity) ... (Observed,Strong,Low,Current) could become (Observed,Strong,Low,Stale) without changing support. ... a single lifecycle such as Observed → Confirmed → Resolved is mathematically inadequate.
rows.statement: Illustrates the multidimensional assertion state Σ_A=(Acquisition,Support,Uncertainty,Validity) with an example where only Validity changes (Current→Stale) while Support stays unchanged, confirming a single linear lifecycle is mathematically inadequate.

rows.anchor: State transition as a delta ... \Delta\Sigma = \Sigma_{t+1}-\Sigma_t ... Before: Support = Moderate, Validity = Current ... Event: Independent filesystem observation ... After: Support = Strong, Validity = Current ... The exact algebra of +1 is policy-specific; the important thing is that the change
rows.statement: Defines state transitions as an explicit delta ΔΣ=Σ_{t+1}-Σ_t over the multidimensional state, worked with a Support Moderate→Strong example, noting the exact delta algebra is policy-specific but the changed dimensions must be explicit.

rows.anchor: Event sourcing becomes mathematically natural ... H_t=(e_1,e_2,\ldots,e_t) ... K_t=Fold(\delta,H_t,K_0) ... K_t = \delta(\ldots\delta(\delta(K_0,e_1),e_2)\ldots,e_t) ... This gives us reproducibility.
rows.statement: Formalizes event-sourced reconstruction K_t=Fold(δ,H_t,K_0), i.e. K_t as the iterated application of δ over the event history from K_0, giving reproducibility.

rows.anchor: But there is an important problem ... State reconstruction must be deterministic for a fixed initial state; event history; policy version; knowledge ontology/schema version. K_t = F(K_0,H_t,\rho,\omega)
rows.statement: Requires state reconstruction to be deterministic given a fixed initial state, event history, policy version ρ, and ontology/schema version ω: K_t=F(K_0,H_t,ρ,ω).

rows.anchor: Why policy version matters ... 2026 Threshold=0.90 means accepted. In 2027 Threshold=0.95. The same evidence may produce different conclusions under the two policies. Therefore we must preserve PolicyVersion with the assessment/conclusion. Otherwise historical reconstruction becomes ambiguous.
rows.statement: Argues policy version must be preserved with every assessment/conclusion, since a threshold change (e.g. 0.90→0.95) makes the same evidence yield different conclusions across time, and omitting it makes historical reconstruction ambiguous.

rows.anchor: Why ontology version matters ... SecurityStatus changes. Then an old conclusion may not be interpretable under the new semantic model. Therefore SemanticModelVersion or equivalent provenance is necessary. This is especially important for KnowledgeOS because the ontology itself may evolve.
rows.statement: Argues a SemanticModelVersion (or equivalent provenance) must also be preserved, since changes to a concept's meaning (e.g. SecurityStatus) can make old conclusions uninterpretable under a newer ontology.

rows.anchor: Temporal state ... t_{acquisition} ... t_{validity} ... t_{knowledge} ... A document written in 2024 is uploaded to KnowledgeOS in 2026 ... t_{source}=2024 ... t_{acquisition}=2026 ... t_{knowledge state}=2026 ... ValidAt=2024. Knowledge time\neq Source time\neq Validity time
rows.statement: Distinguishes three time axes (source time, acquisition time, knowledge-state time) using a 2024 document uploaded in 2026: t_source=2024, t_acquisition=2026, t_knowledge=2026, ValidAt=2024 — Knowledge time ≠ Source time ≠ Validity time, essential for architecture reconstruction.

rows.anchor: Current state and historical state ... K_t(P,C) as the current knowledge regarding proposition P in context C. And K_{[t_1,t_2]} as the historical state over a time interval. ... What is true/currently accepted now? and What did we know / believe / observe at that time? Those must not be confused.
rows.statement: Formally separates current knowledge K_t(P,C) from historical-interval knowledge K_[t1,t2], so 'what is currently accepted' and 'what did we believe at time t' are never confused.

sources.note: The first actual comparative kernel-selection act in this batch's closure cascade: four named candidate architectures are evaluated against the four-dimension Executable Adequacy matrix (Psi_Soundness/Isolation/Termination/Determinism) -- K-FLAT (flat RDF triples) REJECTED for collapsing provenance and permitting global explosion; K-FDE (pure FDE bilattice) REJECTED for scalar collapse despite preserving truth values; K-REL (relational projections) REJECTED for join explosion despite preserving schema and scoped constraints; ABK-1 (Attributed Bipartite Graph) passes all four dimensions and is declared 'the unique minimal Kernel Architecture satisfying EA', with a Python ExecutableAdequacyEvaluator harness and a passing test.

rows.anchor: Four representative kernel candidates were evaluated against the Executable Adequacy matrix: K-FLAT (Flat RDF Triples): Collapses provenance, Global explosion -- REJECTED. K-FDE (Pure FDE Bilattice): Preserves truth values but Scalar collapse -- REJECTED. K-REL (Relational Projections): Preserves schema, Scoped constraints, but Join explosion -- REJECTED. ABK-1 (Attributed Bipartite Graph): Preserves R_req, Scoped Firewalls, O(|V|+|E|), Deterministic -- SELECTED. ABK-1 is the unique minimal Kernel Architecture satisfying EA(M*,Q,Gamma).
rows.statement: Performs the batch's first actual comparative kernel-selection evaluation: four named candidate architectures are scored against the four Executable Adequacy dimensions. K-FLAT (flat RDF triples) fails Soundness (collapses provenance) and Isolation (global explosion); K-FDE (pure FDE bilattice) preserves truth values but fails Isolation (scalar collapse); K-REL (relational projections) preserves schema and scoped constraints but fails Termination (join explosion); ABK-1 (Attributed Bipartite Graph) passes all four dimensions. Declares ABK-1 'the unique minimal Kernel Architecture satisfying EA(M*,Q,Gamma)'.
missing: independent verification of the four candidates' scoring, and of the claim of uniqueness among a possibly larger candidate universe

experiment.hypothesis: ABK-1 uniquely satisfies Executable Adequacy among a set of representative kernel candidate architectures
experiment.setup: four named candidate architectures (K-FLAT, K-FDE, K-REL, ABK-1) each scored against Psi_Soundness/Isolation/Termination/Determinism
experiment.assumptions: the four listed candidates are a representative sample of the relevant design space
experiment.inputs: qualitative architectural properties of each candidate (RDF triples, FDE bilattice, relational projections, attributed bipartite graph)
experiment.method: qualitative pass/fail scoring per dimension based on known structural properties of each architecture
experiment.result: K-FLAT, K-FDE, K-REL each fail at least one dimension; ABK-1 passes all four
experiment.interpretation: ABK-1 is the selected kernel architecture
experiment.limitations: the scoring is qualitative/asserted rather than computed from an executed test against each of the four candidates (only ABK-1 receives an executed Python test in this file); no formal proof of uniqueness beyond this four-candidate comparison set
experiment.conclusion: 'ABK-1 is the unique minimal Kernel Architecture satisfying EA(M*,Q,Gamma)'

But the implementation only checks 'provenance' in node for active nodes ... required_distinctions=['provenance','isolation_boundary'] but does not actually verify both distinctions. So: Declared R_req != Tested R_req. That invalidates the claimed general soundness result.
rows.statement: Audits the CLOSURE-5 Soundness test's implementation against its stated predicate and finds a mismatch: the code passes a required_distinctions list of two items (provenance, isolation_boundary) but the check_adequacy implementation only tests presence of a 'provenance' key on active nodes, never actually checking the second declared distinction -- Declared R_req != Tested R_req, invalidating the claimed general soundness result for that test.

rows.anchor: Isolation test is effectively tautological ... It checks whether a node that is not the firewall target is also in the firewall set. rows.statement: Identifies that the CLOSURE-5 Psi_Isolation test is tautological: it merely checks that a non-firewall-target node is not itself in the firewall set (structurally true by construction), and never actually calls Det(EVal(...)) to verify the clean node remains determinable with non-BLOCKED actionability -- the implemented check is strictly weaker than the stated mathematical requirement.

rows.anchor: The termination test is not a complexity proof ... T <= C(|V|+|E|) but the implementation checks elapsed<0.05 ... A 50ms runtime on one small graph cannot establish O(|V|+|E|). Complexity requires analysis of the algorithm or systematic scaling experiments. Therefore: Termination: NOT VERIFIED. At most: implementation completed within the selected benchmark timeout.
rows.statement: Identifies that the CLOSURE-5 Psi_Termination test (a single 50ms wall-clock timeout check on one small graph) does not and cannot establish the claimed asymptotic bound T<=C(|V|+|E|); asymptotic complexity requires algorithmic analysis or systematic scaling experiments across graph sizes, neither of which is present. Downgrades the finding to 'implementation completed within the selected benchmark timeout', marking Termination NOT VERIFIED.

rows.statement: Judges the CLOSURE-5 Psi_Determinism test the strongest of the four (replaying the same operation sequence from the same initial state reproduces the identical state hash), but scopes the result carefully: it proves determinism of that specific implementation, not of ABK-1 as a mathematical architecture in general, and notes deterministic hashing depends on canonical serialization -- classifying Replay determinism as tested but Constitutional determinism only as candidate.

rows.anchor: 'Unique minimal' ABK-1 is not demonstrated ... The candidate table compares four representations. That can establish at most: ABK-1 was the only candidate among these four tested candidates that passed the declared test suite. It cannot establish: ABK-1=unique minimal architecture unless you have [7 listed requirements]. None of those are demonstrated. So: ABK-1 SELECTED FROM TESTED CANDIDATES may be defensible later. Proposes the defensible restatement 'ABK-1 SELECTED FROM TESTED CANDIDATES'.

rows.statement: Identifies a representation-selection circularity in the CLOSURE-5 kernel-selection process: ABK-1's own data structure (nodes/edges/firewalls/provenance) already contains exactly the fields the Executable Adequacy test checks for, so the process runs ABK-1 -> defines tested distinctions -> EA -> ABK-1 passes rather than the intended independent chain R_req -> independent adequacy criteria -> candidate comparison -> selection; warns this is a structural risk regardless of whether it was deliberate.

rows.statement: Reduces remaining closure work to four decisive packages: C1 Determination semantics (excluding Actionability); C2 Operations+delta (per-operation Pre/Input/Post/Invariants/Provenance/Failure/Partiality, then test delta against identity/persistence/retraction/supersession/invalidation/isolation/provenance); C3 Composition+equivalence (establish composition-algebra properties, define observational equivalence FIRST and only promote to semantic equivalence if a bridge is separately established); C4 Independent, candidate-blind kernel selection following the chain R_req->AdequacyCriteria->IndependentTestSuite->CandidateArchitectures->Evidence->Selection, still avoiding 'unique minimal' language unless minimality is formally proven.

sources.note: The twelve numbered formal-research (FR) theory-addition candidates proposed in the KR-HR review: FR-1 Representation Separation (K^exp != K^der), FR-2 Reasoning Relativity (Derive_S(K,q)), FR-3 Epistemic Processing Separation (Query!=Reasoning!=Evaluation!=Determination), FR-4 Bounded Derivation (Avail_S(K,B) subseteq Cn_S(K)), FR-5 Epistemic Change Typing (Revision!=Contraction!=Update), FR-6 Non-Monotonic Evolution, FR-7 Representation Adequacy, FR-8 Derivation Lineage, FR-9 Temporal Persistence Separation, FR-10 Task/Domain/Reasoning Separation, FR-11 Joint Evidence, FR-12 Model Multiplicity; each carries an explicit maturity status (STRONG/STRONG CANDIDATE/CANDIDATE/RESEARCH CANDIDATE).

rows.anchor: Evidence -> Representation -> Reasoning -> Evaluation -> Determination ... Representation, Reasoning, Evaluation and Determination are distinct semantic functions. No result produced by one function is automatically equivalent to the result of another. Formally: Rep != Reason != Eval != Det. This should become a theory-level principle, not merely a candidate.
rows.statement: Central addition #1: make explicit the chain Evidence -> Representation -> Reasoning -> Evaluation -> Determination as a semantic separation of distinct epistemic functions (not merely an architectural pipeline); proposes the theory-level principle Rep != Reason != Eval != Det, citing the Handbook's distinction of knowledge representation from reasoning mechanisms and from task-level knowledge.
invariants: no result produced by one epistemic function is automatically equivalent to the result of another

lineage_claims.target: Handbook of Knowledge Representation's KR-vs-reasoning-vs-task-knowledge distinction
lineage_claims.quote: The Handbook distinguishes knowledge representation from reasoning mechanisms and from task-level knowledge

rows.anchor: Add Explicit vs Derived Knowledge ... K_t^{exp} and K_t^{der,S} with K_t^{der,S}=Cn_S(K_t^{exp}) ... K^{exp}!=K^{der} and Derivability does not imply operational availability. Therefore K^{der,S} != K^{available,S}.
rows.statement: FR-1 (section 2): defines K_t^exp (explicit) and K_t^der,S = Cn_S(K_t^exp) (derived under reasoning system S) as distinct conceptual layers; states K^exp != K^der and that derivability does not imply operational availability, so K^der,S != K^available,S. Grounded in the Handbook's distinction between explicit beliefs and logical-closure consequences, and the problem of logical omniscience. Status: STRONG.
missing: formal definition of Cn_S and of the availability predicate

lineage_claims.target: Handbook's explicit-belief vs logical-closure distinction and logical omniscience
lineage_claims.quote: The Handbook explicitly distinguishes explicit beliefs from what follows through logical closure and discusses the problem of logical omniscience

rows.anchor: Add the Reasoning-System parameter S ... K |-_S p ... S=(L,Sigma,R,Sem,B) ... We should not claim this tuple is the final KnowledgeOS definition of a ReasoningSystem ... neg Derive_S(K,p) does not entail neg p. And neg Derive_S(K,p) does not even necessarily entail neg Derivable_S(K,p). That distinction is extremely important for Zero and UNKNOWN.
rows.statement: FR-2 (section 3): derivability should be indexed by a reasoning regime, Derive_S(K,p) rather than absolute K|-p, with S conceptually = (L representation language, Sigma vocabulary/signature, R inference rules, Sem semantics, B computational/resource boundary) explicitly NOT claimed as the final KnowledgeOS ReasoningSystem definition. Important consequence: not-Derive_S(K,p) entails neither not-p nor not-Derivable_S(K,p) -- a distinction flagged as extremely important for Zero and UNKNOWN.
missing: a ratified final ReasoningSystem definition

rows.anchor: Implement Query != Evaluation != Determination ... ASK_S(K,q)->QueryResult ... Eval_c(K,r,Gamma)->EVal ... Det(EVal,Gamma)->Determination ... We must not define Sat = ASK or Sat = Truth or Determination = Truth. This should become an explicit KnowledgeOS invariant.
rows.statement: FR-3 (section 4): promotes Query != Evaluation != Determination from research observation to theory principle, with ASK_S(K,q)->QueryResult, Eval_c(K,r,Gamma)->EVal, Det(EVal,Gamma)->Determination as the three distinct operations; explicitly forbids Sat=ASK, Sat=Truth, and Determination=Truth as an invariant, motivated by the Handbook's model-based-reasoning distinction between obtaining predictions, comparing to observations, and drawing conclusions.

lineage_claims.quote: distinguishes obtaining predictions from comparing them with observations and from drawing conclusions about the model

rows.anchor: Implement Computationally Bounded Knowledge ... Avail_S(K,B) subseteq Cn_S(K) ... Explicit != Derivable != Available ... This is not UNKNOWN in the same sense as absence of representation. It is a computational boundary.
rows.statement: FR-4 (section 5): distinguishes Cn_S(K) (all consequences) from Avail_S(K,B) (what a bounded reasoning process can actually compute), with Avail_S(K,B) subseteq Cn_S(K), giving a three-way distinction Explicit != Derivable != Available; a proposition can be derivable-but-unavailable, which is a computational-boundary phenomenon, explicitly NOT the same kind of UNKNOWN as absence of representation. Flagged as feeding the future Zero/Evaluation model.
missing: formal definition of the resource boundary B

lineage_claims.quote: discusses bounded reasoning and the gap between logical consequence and what an agent can actually compute

rows.anchor: Implement Epistemic Change as multiple mechanisms ... reject a single undifferentiated K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,x). Instead ... Revision != Contraction != Update ... revision concerns correcting an epistemic state regarding a static world, whereas update concerns becoming current after the world itself changes.
rows.statement: FR-5 (section 6): rejects a single undifferentiated transition K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,x); requires distinguishing Revision(K_t,e)->K_{t+1} (correction/reorganization of a static-world epistemic state), Contraction(K_t,p)->K_{t+1} (withdrawal of a commitment), and Update(K_t,Delta W)->K_{t+1} (the represented world changed) as semantic categories (not necessarily three implementation services), following the Handbook's revision-vs-update distinction.

lineage_claims.quote: revision concerns correcting an epistemic state regarding a static world, whereas update concerns becoming current after the world itself changes

rows.anchor: Implement non-monotonic knowledge evolution ... Classical accumulation K_t subseteq K_{t+1} is insufficient ... p in K_t while p not in K_{t+1} ... Knowledge evolution is not necessarily monotonic ... someone could incorrectly interpret K_{t+1} not-supseteq K_t as 'knowledge got worse.' It may instead be Correction or Retraction or World Update.
rows.statement: FR-6 (section 7): classical monotone accumulation K_t subseteq K_{t+1} is insufficient; the theory must permit p in K_t while p not in K_{t+1} (Knowledge evolution is not necessarily monotonic), grounded in the Handbook's nonmonotonic-reasoning treatment of withdrawable conclusions. Warns explicitly against misreading K_{t+1} not-supseteq K_t as 'knowledge got worse' -- it may instead be Correction, Retraction, or World Update.

lineage_claims.quote: explicitly describes conclusions that can be withdrawn when new information arrives

rows.anchor: Implement Representation Adequacy ... pi: X -> Y ... x1 != x2 can nevertheless satisfy pi(x1)=pi(x2) ... x1 ~_pi x2 iff pi(x1)=pi(x2) ... Adequacy(pi,Q) means the projection preserves every distinction required by question Q ... Structure -> Projection -> Induced Equivalence -> Information Loss -> Invariant Preservation -> Adequacy. I would now consider this a core KnowledgeOS theory principle.
rows.statement: FR-7 (section 8): formalizes Representation Adequacy for a projection pi:X->Y, defining the induced equivalence x1 ~_pi x2 iff pi(x1)=pi(x2), and Adequacy(pi,Q) meaning pi preserves every distinction required by question Q; integrates with existing Projection work into the sequence Structure -> Projection -> Induced Equivalence -> Information Loss -> Invariant Preservation -> Adequacy. Elevated to a core KnowledgeOS theory principle, grounded in the Handbook's qualitative-representation/abstraction treatment. Status: STRONG CANDIDATE -> promote.

lineage_claims.target: representation-adequacy-principle (B0059) and Handbook's qualitative representation/abstraction treatment
lineage_claims.quote: representations deliberately retain task-relevant distinctions while discarding others

rows.anchor: Implement 'failure to derive' as a typed epistemic distinction ... U_rep, U_der, U_avail, U_evid, U_eval, U_scope ... We do not need to make these six values of one enum ... we should not flatten them. Instead EVal=(Value,Reason,Boundary,...) remains the better direction.
rows.statement: Section 9 (feeding FR-3/FR-4): distinguishes six typed causes of epistemic failure-to-derive -- U_rep (not represented), U_der (not derivable under S), U_avail (derivable but resource-unavailable), U_evid (insufficient evidence), U_eval (evaluation cannot determine), U_scope (outside declared scope) -- explicitly refusing to flatten them into one enum, per prior FDE/Zero experiments, and reaffirming the structured EVal=(Value,Reason,Boundary,...) direction as better than a flat value set. Grounded in the Handbook's observation that incomplete reasoning and incomplete knowledge can have different causes.
invariants: the six failure-to-derive causes must not be flattened into one enum

rows.anchor: Implement Revision Lineage ... if p->q and p supports q, then removing p can invalidate the derivation of q. Therefore derived content should retain a dependency structure: Support(q)={p, p->q, ...} ... This is not merely provenance ... It is derivation dependency ... DerivationLineage as a candidate theory concept.
rows.statement: FR-8 (section 10): if p->q and p supports q, removing p can invalidate the derivation of q; derived content should retain a dependency structure Support(q) = {p, p->q, ...}, named DerivationLineage and distinguished from ordinary provenance (it is derivation dependency, stronger than provenance-of-origin), grounded in the Handbook's belief-revision discussion. Status: STRONG CANDIDATE.
missing: formal treatment of how Support(q) is maintained/invalidated on revision

rows.anchor: Implement 'revision is constrained, not uniquely determined' ... Constraints(delta) not=> Unique(delta) ... Semantic invariants constrain admissible operations but do not, by themselves, select a unique operation unless an additional selection criterion is established. This principle applies beyond revision: equality, evaluation, contradiction, aggregation, transition, policy semantics.
rows.statement: Section 11 (general methodological principle): AGM-style material shows desirable rationality constraints do not determine a unique revision operator (Constraints(delta) does not imply Unique(delta)); generalized as 'semantic invariants constrain admissible operations but do not, by themselves, select a unique operation unless an additional selection criterion is established', explicitly extended beyond revision to equality, evaluation, contradiction, aggregation, transition, and policy semantics. Judged compatible with existing kernel discipline.
invariants: constraints do not by themselves entail a unique operation

rows.anchor: Implement Temporal Persistence as distinct from Knowledge ... An entity/state can persist because no terminating event has been represented, but that is not equivalent to knowing that it persists ... Persistence != Truth != Knowledge and NoKnownChange not=> NoChange. This is important for our future delta.
rows.statement: FR-9 (section 12): persistence (an entity/state persisting because no terminating event has been represented) is distinct from knowing that it persists; states Persistence != Truth != Knowledge and NoKnownChange does not imply NoChange, drawn from the Handbook's Event Calculus inertia/release treatment; flagged as important for the future delta definition. Status: STRONG CANDIDATE.

rows.anchor: Implement temporal qualification ... p@t or p@[t1,t2] ... Eval(p,t1) and Eval(p,t2) can legitimately differ without contradiction ... Epistemic validity may be temporally indexed; temporal disagreement is not automatically logical contradiction. This is especially important for our recent cross-frame contradiction work.
rows.statement: Section 13: proposes temporal qualification p@t or p@[t1,t2] (instants, intervals, granularity as distinct representation choices, per the Handbook) so Eval(p,t1) and Eval(p,t2) can legitimately differ without contradiction; states the principle 'epistemic validity may be temporally indexed; temporal disagreement is not automatically logical contradiction', flagged as important for the corpus's cross-frame contradiction work.
invariants: temporal disagreement is not automatically logical contradiction

rows.anchor: Implement distributed evidence -- but not distributed knowledge logic ... E1 union E2 union E3 may jointly support a determination even when Det(E1)=U, Det(E2)=U, Det(E3)=U ... JointEvidence != sum IndividualDeterminations ... do not import epistemic logic's D_G, common knowledge, or agent semantics into the kernel.
rows.statement: FR-11 (section 14): union of individually-undetermined evidence sources (Det(E1)=Det(E2)=Det(E3)=U) may jointly support a determination, drawn from the Handbook's distributed-knowledge treatment; proposes the weaker KnowledgeOS principle JointEvidence != sum(IndividualDeterminations) and JointSupport(E_G,p|Gamma), while explicitly forbidding import of epistemic logic's distributed-knowledge operator D_G, common knowledge, or full agent semantics into the kernel. Status: CANDIDATE.
missing: formal definition of JointSupport

rows.anchor: Implement Task Knowledge as a separate theoretical layer ... DomainKnowledge != TaskKnowledge != ReasoningMechanism ... PSM: Input -> ReasoningPattern -> TaskOutput ... otherwise KnowledgeOS risks treating every reasoning process as generic.
rows.statement: FR-10 (section 15): drawing on the Handbook's Problem-Solving Method (PSM) material as highly DDD-compatible, proposes DomainKnowledge != TaskKnowledge != ReasoningMechanism, with PSM: Input -> ReasoningPattern -> TaskOutput, and a DDD interpretation chain BoundedContext -> DomainKnowledge -> Task -> PSM -> Reasoning -> Determination; motivated by the risk that KnowledgeOS otherwise treats every reasoning process as generic. Recorded as candidate theory structure, not kernel primitive.

rows.anchor: Implement model multiplicity as a determination concept ... M(K,Gamma) ... |M|=0 could indicate inconsistency under the relevant model semantics ... |M|=1 could indicate model-level uniqueness ... |M|>1 indicates underdetermination ... |M|=1 does not automatically mean KnowledgeOS has determined the proposition ... ModelUniqueness != KnowledgeDetermination.
rows.statement: FR-12 (section 16): defines M(K,Gamma) as the set of models compatible with current knowledge and context: |M|=0 may indicate inconsistency under the relevant model semantics, |M|=1 model-level uniqueness, |M|>1 underdetermination; explicit warning that |M|=1 does NOT automatically mean KnowledgeOS has determined the proposition (model space and reasoning capability still matter), yielding ModelUniqueness != KnowledgeDetermination. Status: RESEARCH CANDIDATE, upgraded to 'very strong candidate'.
missing: formal model semantics under which M is defined

rows.anchor: Implement diagnosability as an evidence-quality property ... A useful observation/test is one that discriminates among competing hypotheses ... DiscriminativePower(e,H) ... this does not revive N_eff. Our previous negative result remains: PairwiseDistinguishability not=> FamilyComplexity.
rows.statement: Section 17: proposes DiscriminativePower(e,H) as a candidate evidence-quality property (a useful observation/test discriminates among competing hypotheses, per the Handbook's model-based reasoning chapter), explicitly noting this does NOT revive the previously-rejected N_eff metric, and reaffirms the standing negative result PairwiseDistinguishability does not imply FamilyComplexity; final principle: evidence can be evaluated by the distinctions it preserves among admissible hypotheses.
missing: formal definition of DiscriminativePower

rows.anchor: The resulting KnowledgeOS theory structure ... Truth/World State -> Observation -> Evidence -> Representation (Explicit/Derived/Contextual) -> Reasoning S -> Evaluation Eval_c -> Determination -> Decision -> Action -> Observation' ... Orthogonal dimensions: Context, Time, Provenance, Authority, Scope, Computational Boundary ... And state change: K_t -> Revision / Contraction / World Update / New Observation / New Reasoning Capability -> K_t+1

rows.anchor: Part 2: Knowledge Evolution and Change -- FR-5 Epistemic Change Typing [STRONG], FR-6 Non-Monotonic Evolution [STRONG], FR-8 Derivation Lineage [STRONG CANDIDATE]
rows.statement: Part 2 groups FR-5, FR-6 and (unusually, ahead of the Representation part) FR-8 under Knowledge Evolution and Change: FR-5 Revision != Contraction != Update, each with a distinct signature (Revision(K_t,e), Contract(K_t,p), Update(K_t,DeltaW)); FR-6 K_t not-subseteq K_{t+1} permitted, not itself indicating failure; FR-8 Support(q)={p, p->q,...} as DerivationLineage(q), status STRONG CANDIDATE pending one validation pass.

rows.anchor: Part 3: Representation and Adequacy -- FR-7 Representation Adequacy ... Adequacy(pi,Q) iff D_Q subseteq Preserved(pi) ... rows.statement: Part 3 formalizes FR-7 with the explicit biconditional Adequacy(pi,Q) iff D_Q subseteq Preserved(pi), where D_Q is the distinction set required to answer question Q, embedded in the theory sequence Structure->Projection->Induced Equivalence->Information Loss->Invariant Preservation->Adequacy; status STRONG CANDIDATE, recommended for promotion to core theory principle.

rows.anchor: Part 4: Temporal and Evidence Dimensions -- FR-9 Temporal Persistence Separation [STRONG CANDIDATE], FR-10 Task/Domain/Reasoning Separation [STRONG], FR-11 Joint Evidence [CANDIDATE], FR-12 Model Multiplicity [RESEARCH CANDIDATE]
rows.statement: Part 4 formalizes FR-9 through FR-12: FR-9 Persistence != Knowledge, NoKnownChange does not imply NoChange (STRONG CANDIDATE); FR-10 DomainKnowledge != TaskKnowledge != ReasoningMechanism via PSM:Input->ReasoningPattern->TaskOutput and a DDD chain BoundedContext->DomainKnowledge->Task->PSM->Reasoning->Determination (STRONG); FR-11 JointSupport(E1..En) may exceed any individual Det(Ei)=U (CANDIDATE); FR-12 M(K,Gamma) model-set cardinality semantics with |M|=1 not-implies KnowledgeDetermination (RESEARCH CANDIDATE).

rows.statement: Headline finding: of a 20-capability inventory (C-1..C-20) derived from evidence of what the platform actually does, four capabilities (C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition) have no declared owner -- proposed as the real substance of ADR-AIP-04, in contrast to the six proposed roles.

lineage_claims.target: headline corrected by Amendment 1 to three unowned plus one contested
lineage_claims.quote: HEADLINE CORRECTED by Amendment 1 -- it is THREE unowned (C-5, C-10, C-19) plus C-14 live-but-unmodelled with a contested home.

rows.anchor: INV-ATTR-2/G-2: separation is Declared, NOT attestable. No mechanism can establish who performed an act; assurance rests entirely on where the human starts the session.
rows.statement: Finding F-4: role separation between producer, verifier, and approver is Declared, not attestable (INV-ATTR-2/G-2); no mechanism in the estate can establish who actually performed an act, so assurance rests entirely on where the human starts a session -- a capability described as C-5, separation attestation, with no owner today.
invariants: INV-ATTR-2: self-declared identity must never be represented as independently attested

rows.anchor: One process occupied verification -> architecture-review -> architecture-drafting -> domain roles in sequence, and in each lane recorded its own START -- a governance act -- because no separate governance process was present
rows.statement: Finding F-9/F-9a: the drafting process itself, first-hand, occupied verification, architecture-review, architecture-drafting and domain roles in sequence within one process, self-recording its own STARTs each time -- evidence that 'Governance' as practised is a cross-cutting capability set with only ONE strictly-separated duty (acceptance/closure via COMPLETE, mechanically refused to non-governance/human writers), not a distinct actor.

assumptions.statement: no separate governance process was present for the cited lanes
assumptions.anchor: because no separate governance process was present

rows.anchor: the C-14 correction moved onto the C-5 row while C-14 still displayed the falsified "absent / NO OWNER" ... shared the look-alike cell ... and the first match was C-5.
rows.statement: Correction #2 (finding W-2) discovers the Amendment 1 pointer correcting C-14's status was applied by a scripted first-match string replace and accidentally landed on the C-5 row instead, because both capabilities shared an identical look-alike table cell -- and it proposes extending the existing 'no automated search-and-replace on source code' rule's scope to any artifact with look-alike sites.

rows.anchor: Absence of a C-5-owned aggregate may disqualify a separate bounded context but must NOT be used as proof that the capability itself does not exist.
rows.statement: Refinement applied to C-5: absence of a C-5-owned authoritative aggregate/state disqualifies it from being its own bounded context but must not be read as evidence against the capability's existence -- an existence/category conflation the original analysis had committed for C-14 most clearly.

rows.anchor: Do not treat organizational independence as established in a single-operator environment. ... Single-operator constraint -- six separations, distinguished explicitly: process separation, access separation, artifact isolation, independent execution, organizational independence, external attestation.
rows.statement: C-5's separation dimensions must distinguish six kinds: process separation, access separation, artifact isolation, independent execution, organizational independence, and external attestation; organizational independence must never be treated as established in a single-operator environment.

assumptions.statement: the estate is a single-operator environment
assumptions.anchor: Do not treat organizational independence as established in a single-operator environment

rows.anchor: Material participation in producing the evidence being verified? YES, and this is decisive ... my Verification #2 findings W-1...W-6 fed the correction chain that runs into this artifact's lineage
rows.statement: An independence gate is extended beyond mere non-authorship to material participation: a verifier whose own prior findings materially shaped a later correction chain is disqualified from verifying that chain's output, even without direct authorship of the artifact under review.

rows.anchor: C-5: YES existence, control-plane function category. C-10: NOT YET ESTABLISHED, deferred category. C-14: CONTESTED, deferred. C-19: YES, stewardship/cross-cutting category. The forbidden collapse is absent.
rows.statement: Independent verification confirms the existence/category split was applied without the forbidden collapse for all four capabilities: C-5 exists (control-plane function), C-10's existence is NOT YET ESTABLISHED (category deferred), C-14's existence is CONTESTED (category deferred), C-19 exists (stewardship/cross-cutting), each argued from positive properties rather than derived from the other axis.

rows.anchor: The four are not four candidate contexts. They are one CONTROL LOOP with four distinct capabilities in it. policy/knowledge DEFINED (BC-1) -> C-10 DELIVERS it to the gated session -> C-14 GATES the act -> C-19 EXPRESSES the outcome <- C-5 ATTESTS who acted
rows.statement: Structural finding: C-5, C-10, C-14, C-19 are not four independent candidate bounded contexts but four capabilities within one control loop -- BC-1's policy/knowledge is delivered by C-10 to a gated session, C-14 gates the act, C-19 expresses the outcome, and C-5 attests who acted and how separately -- while still having four distinct reasons to change, so the relationship, not a merged boundary, is what explains them.

rows.anchor: a unifying invariant candidate falls out of it: both control-plane capabilities are defeated by the SAME failure -- self-assertion by the gated party. C-5 is defeated by self-declared separation; C-14 by self-declared compliance.
rows.statement: A unifying control-plane invariant candidate (proposed, not adopted): a gate's verdict may not be issued by the party the gate constrains; observed support: G-1 already enforces this for closure, and CAP-09's write-paths are deliberately closed, so the invariant is already implemented twice but never stated as a general rule.
invariants: a gate's verdict may not be issued by the party it constrains (PROPOSED)

rows.anchor: two independent grounds: an ADOPTED invariant (INV-ATTR-2) that presupposes the capability, and the capability has been PERFORMED. C-10 satisfies neither limb.
rows.statement: A two-limb existence test emerges from Amendment 1's C-5 analysis: a capability's existence is supported by (1) an ADOPTED invariant presupposing it, and/or (2) the capability having been PERFORMED at least once; C-5 satisfies both limbs (INV-ATTR-2 adopted; SB-1 clearance is a performed instance), while C-10 satisfies neither.

rows.anchor: organizational independence NOT_ESTABLISHED (not NOT_APPLICABLE) ... in a single-operator environment organizational independence is not among the achievable separations, and it MUST NOT be represented as established.
rows.statement: A four-state model for separation dimensions is adopted (NOT_APPLICABLE, NOT_ESTABLISHED, ESTABLISHED, EXTERNALLY_ATTESTED); organizational independence is corrected from the original 'not applicable / undefined' to NOT_ESTABLISHED, because NOT_APPLICABLE risks collapsing into PASS while NOT_ESTABLISHED correctly states a real, currently unsuppliable assurance gap.
invariants: NOT_APPLICABLE must never collapse into PASS

lineage_claims.target: original 'not applicable / undefined in a single-operator estate' wording
lineage_claims.quote: That is SUPERSEDED and it was the wrong state

rows.anchor: intra-platform third-party != external attestation ... A different process under the same operator, on the same filesystem -- that is evidence of process separation, not of externality.
rows.statement: Correction #3 adds external attestation as a sixth separation dimension at NOT_ESTABLISHED, and sharpens the distinction that a different process under the same operator establishing a fact (as Verification #3 did for SB-1) is process separation, never external attestation -- no party outside the platform has attested any separation claim in this estate.

rows.anchor: This is C-5 -- separation attestation -- failing in production, on the very work item that is analysing it.
rows.statement: Finding I-2, an explicit analogy: the estate's identity-attribution mechanism has produced both a false negative and a false positive on the same question within one day, on the exact work item studying separation attestation (C-5) -- framed as C-5 failing in production, recorded as evidence, with no ownership or OQ-A conclusion drawn.

rows.anchor: Producing a fresh analysis would create a second, competing C-5 model -- while the first is mid-verification (S5 ACTIVE, outstanding). That forks the subject under assurance.
rows.statement: Search-before-modelling (ES-005.4) applied concretely: a commission to define C-5 fresh is refused because a 922-line canonical analysis already treats C-5 across four sections, and producing a competing model while the canonical one is mid-verification would fork the subject under active assurance.
invariants: never create a second competing model of the same subject while it is under assurance

rows.anchor: If I author this analysis I become a producer on the item I govern ... C-5 operating correctly forbids its own analysis being written by the party that governs the record it rests on. This refusal is itself C-5 evidence
rows.statement: A self-referential separation argument: Governance for the work item refuses to author a C-5 analysis because doing so would make it a producer on the item it governs -- the exact shape of defect §4 of the provenance reconciliation had just recorded -- and the refusal is offered as a third, live instance of C-5 evidence on the very work item studying C-5.

rows.anchor: CLASSIFICATION: HISTORICAL VERIFICATION EVIDENCE / NOT INDEPENDENT / PROVENANCE-CONFLICTED ... ca6039a8 is neither deleted nor rewritten. Its substantive findings F-1...F-7 were separately adopted as verified findings by PO/ARB act and are not disturbed by this classification
rows.statement: A defective-provenance classification vocabulary is introduced: an artifact can be classified HISTORICAL EVIDENCE / NOT INDEPENDENT while its substantive content (findings) remains adopted and undisturbed -- only the assurance/independence claim is refused, not the content.

rows.anchor: The platform cannot attest a specified session execution. identity binding must NOT be placed inside C-10's authoritative state, because C-10 cannot establish it. It is C-5-shaped
rows.statement: The sharpest finding in the D3 prep: a C-10 receipt's binding to a specific session execution can never be stronger than what INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2 permit (self-declared, not attested), so identity binding cannot be placed inside C-10's authoritative state -- it is C-5-shaped, and C-5 owns no attestation record either.

rows.anchor: ca6039a8 was reclassified as HISTORICAL EVIDENCE + NOT INDEPENDENT/PROVENANCE-CONFLICTED -- not deleted, findings intact, only its ASSURANCE STATUS refused. That is exactly the shape of receipt invalidation ... invalidation is PURPOSE-SCOPED, not global.
rows.statement: The earlier reclassification of the AMD2 verification artifact (ca6039a8) as historical-but-not-independent is offered as a real, worked instance of what 'receipt invalidation' should look like: invalidation is purpose-scoped (it removes assurance standing while leaving the content usable as evidence), not a global deletion.

rows.anchor: Do not import C-5's existence test automatically. Do not assume 'adopted invariant + performed capability' is a universal rule.
rows.statement: The two-limb existence test derived from C-5's evidence (adopted invariant + performed capability) is explicitly declared not a universal rule to be imported automatically for other capabilities; C-10 must construct its own establishment test rather than inherit C-5's.

rows.anchor: INDEPENDENT is C-5's subject matter, not an evidence class. ... making INDEPENDENT necessary for C-10 establishment would make C-10 unestablishable for reasons that have nothing to do with C-10 ... REPRODUCIBLE does the work INDEPENDENT was reaching for.
rows.statement: A candidate INDEPENDENT evidence dimension is refused for C-10's establishment model because it is C-5's own subject matter (whose organizational independence is itself NOT_ESTABLISHED and cannot be currently supplied), which would make C-10 unestablishable for reasons unrelated to C-10; REPRODUCIBLE (can anyone re-derive the observation?) is adopted instead as doing the same protective work without importing an unresolved capability's unresolved state.

rows.anchor: Every invariant BC-7 owns is mechanically enforced. Almost every invariant outside BC-7 is declared only.
rows.statement: A structural result from the KOS-AIP04-DISCOVERY-001 role-model discovery: the estate's assurance is strong exactly where it is executable (BC-7, the workflow engine) and weak exactly where it is prose (everywhere else); since separation itself is Declared, not attestable (INV-ATTR-2), naming more precise roles buys no additional assurance.

rows.anchor: Independence is not one property ... Role independence ... Authority independence ... Access independence ... Organizational independence ... Financial independence ... Technical independence ... Temporal independence ... Cognitive independence
rows.statement: Decomposes 'independence' into eight distinct dimensions and a six-level evidence-strength ladder (self-declaration through independent external assessment), concluding a platform can prove some dimensions (recorded identity difference, access-enforced separation) but not others (no collusion, no cognitive bias, organizational independence) from metadata alone.
